questions.question: A region in India is characterized by receiving very scanty rainfall (less than 70 cm annually) and experiences extreme temperatures, with very hot days and cold nights. The natural vegetation here consists mainly of thorny bushes and scrubs, with long roots and waxy leaves. Which region and vegetation type does this description best fit?

options.explanation: Western Ghats have high rainfall and tropical evergreen forests
Himalayan region has different climate and vegetation

options.text: Rajasthan Desert - Thorny Bushes and Scrubs
options.explanation: Rajasthan Desert matches the description given
North-Eastern India has different climate and vegetation

questions.explanation: The described conditions (scanty rainfall, extreme temperatures, thorny vegetation) are characteristic of arid or semi-arid regions, most prominently the Rajasthan Desert where thorny bushes and scrubs are adapted to water scarcity.

questions.question: If you ascend from the plains of North India towards the higher altitudes of the Himalayan mountain range, how would the natural vegetation typically change due to variations in climate?

options.text: From Thorny bushes to Tropical Evergreen forests.
options.explanation: This sequence does not match the change with altitude in the Himalayas

options.text: From Tropical Deciduous forests to Coniferous and Alpine vegetation.
options.explanation: This sequence correctly describes the change in vegetation with increasing altitude

options.text: From Desert vegetation to Mangrove forests.
options.explanation: This sequence is not relevant to the Himalayan mountain range

options.text: From Coniferous forests to Tropical Deciduous forests.
options.explanation: This sequence is the opposite of what occurs with increasing altitude in the Himalayas

questions.explanation: As altitude increases, temperature decreases and rainfall patterns change. The plains often have tropical deciduous forests, which gradually give way to coniferous forests (like pine, deodar) and then alpine vegetation (grasses, shrubs) at higher altitudes in the Himalayas.
